messages:
Priya K: Quick question — can we consolidate the lightweight probe agent and the full bench runner into a single orchestration flow? thinking about faster admission cycles.
Ada L: Short answer: maybe, but tradeoffs. probes are cheap & fast, benches are heavy & sample-rich.
Ryan M: We need to separate lifecycle: probes run on ingest path (slo <500ms), bench runs async on reserved pools. Merging risks blocking intake.
Priya K: Agreed, but duplication of sampling logic is annoying. Can we share the sampler component and have two runners? sampler->fanout(probe, bench)
Marta S: That seems ok. Sampler must export deterministic seeds and metadata (profile hash, seq distributions) so bench results are reproducible.
Ada L: Also need clear contract for failure modes: probe failure -> reject admit? bench failure -> mark as degraded, don't block.
Jules: I'd add a 'sanity' micro-bench that runs quick quantized perf checks (2-3 inputs) on the same runner as probe. Helps catch obvious regressions.
Priya K: example config I'm imagining:
```
sampler:
  strategy: stratified
  seeds: 42
runners:
  - name: probe
    timeout_ms: 300
  - name: microbench
    timeout_ms: 2000
  - name: fullbench
    schedule: async
```
Ryan M: Implementation detail: keep probe path in the entry gateway to preserve latency SLOs. Microbench can be local but must be rate-limited to avoid impacting production GPUs.
Marta S: Also quantized binaries can behave differently; microbench should run on the same binary/profile that will serve in Dedicated, else results lie.
Ada L: On compatibility checks: we should compute a lightweight fingerprint (arch, dims, ops) and gate on known incompatible ops before any runner triggers.
Priya K: How do we expose signals? PR suggestion: sampler emits a "gate signal" object stored in registry with fields: [fingerprint, probe_result, microbench_result, bench_job_id]
Jules: +1. Also add a TTL to bench_job_id so registry doesn't accumulate stuck jobs.
onboard-bot: build/trigger: bench-runner queued (job 4321) — microbench scheduled
Priya K: Next steps: Ryan/Marta can draft minimal contract for sampler -> runners (input/output JSON schema), Ada/Jules will sketch failure handling. I'll collate and write a follow-up RFC.
Ada L: SGTM. Suggest we include a simple replay mode to run microbench/bench on historical samples for regression debugging.
Ryan M: I'll put a rough sketch in the eng-ml doc folder today. tagging @Marta S for runtime constraints.
Marta S: Thanks, will review. :thumbsup:
